title: Grand Duchy of Würzburg
capsule: The Grand Duchy of Würzburg was a short-lived Napoleonic satellite state carved from the former Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg and granted to Archduke Ferdinand of Austria as compensation for his loss of Tuscany under the Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805). Ferdinand I, its sole ruler, joined the Confederation of the Rhine on 30 September 1806 and implemented Napoleonic legal and administrative reforms, including the Code Napoléon. Following Napoleon's defeat at the Battle of Leipzig (October 1813), Ferdinand renounced the French alliance, and an Austrian-Bavarian treaty of 3 June 1814 transferred the territory to the Kingdom of Bavaria. Ferdinand was subsequently restored to Tuscany by the Congress of Vienna.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. As a formally constituted Napoleonic state with clear treaty boundaries, the Grand Duchy's territory is well documented; its geographic extent coincides closely with the former prince-bishopric and is unambiguous.
